"**Mama's Broken Heart**" is a song recorded by American country music artist Miranda Lambert. It was released on January 14, 2013 as the fourth single from Lambert's album, _Four the Record_ (2011). "Mama's Broken Heart" was written by Brandy Clark, Shane McAnally, and Kacey Musgraves, and is about a woman losing control after a break-up and ignoring her mother's advice on dealing with such a situation.
The song garnered a positive reception from critics who praised the production and Lambert's delivery of the lyrics. "Mama's Broken Heart" peaked at number 2 on both the _Billboard_Country Airplay and Hot Country Songs charts respectively. It also charted at number 20 on the Hot 100, her fourth top 40 hit on that chart. The song was certified Platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America and has sold 1,960,000 copies in the United States as of September 2015. It achieved similar chart success in Canada, peaking at number one on the Country chart and number 30 on the Canadian Hot 100.
The accompanying music video for the song was directed by Trey Fanjoy.

"Mama's Broken Heart" is a moderate uptempo song in the key of E minor[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-2) written by Brandy Clark, Shane McAnally, and Kacey Musgraves. The song's female narrator acts out as she struggles with a break-up, which leads people to begin taking notice of her behavior ("Word got around to the barflies and the Baptists"). When her mother finds out, she responds by scolding her daughter and telling her to regain her composure ("Run and hide your crazy and start actin’ like a lady"). The second verse states that the narrator sacrifices her "spotless reputation" in favor of "revenge," which is in contrast with the way her mother's generation handled such situations ("Where you get a grip and bite your lip just to save a little face"), but ultimately she takes matters into her own hands because "[it isn't her] mama's broken heart."
Lambert, in an interview with Taste of Country, said that "Mama's Broken Heart" was the one song on _Four the Record_ she couldn't live without, and that she can relate to the character in the song: "I think we all have at some point or another. Mostly when we’re young. Especially crazy teenage love — you think the world is ending if you break up." She expressed that when she first heard it, "she knew it was special" and wished she had been the one to write it.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-3)

Musgraves, who grew up with Lambert, was reluctant to give her old friend the song, who was pitched it without Musgraves' consent. At her wedding, Lambert asked if Musgraves was going to record the song or if she could have it. Lambert said she had to "actually beg for this song." Musgraves gave it to her on the stipulation that she could sing background vocals, which she did.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-Musgraves-4) Tensions lingered between the two singers over the song, which Musgraves said she resolved when bringing Lambert into the collaborative process on her 2026 album, _Middle of Nowhere_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-5)
The song received favorable reviews from critics. Ben Foster of Country Universe praised the track, referring favorably to its "deceptively deep" lyrics, Lambert's delivery, and an "engaging [and] off-beat arrangement." Foster rated the song an A, and dubbed it Lambert's best single since 2010's "The House That Built Me."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-6) Taste of Country's Billy Dukes awarded the song 4 and 1/2 stars out of 5, comparing it favorably to Lambert's previous hits "Kerosene" and "Gunpowder & Lead" and favorably commenting on the sparse yet suspenseful nature of the production.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-7)

## Commercial performance
[edit]
"Mama's Broken Heart" debuted at number 54 on the U.S. _Billboard_Country Airplay chart for the week ending January 5, 2013, and debuted at number 46 on the U.S. _Billboard_Hot Country Songs chart for the week ending January 12, 2013. It also debuted at number 89 on the U.S. _Billboard_Hot 100 chart for the week of February 9, 2013, and at number 76 on the Canadian Hot 100 chart for the week of February 9, 2013. The song became Lambert's highest-peaking single on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, reaching number 20 until 2014's "[Somethin' Bad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somethin'_Bad "Somethin' Bad")" made it her second highest-peaking single on that chart.
The song has sold 1,960,000 copies in the US as of September 2015.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-sales-8)
The music video was directed by Trey Fanjoy and premiered in March 2013.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-9)

"**Mama's Broken Heart**" is a song recorded by American country music artist Miranda Lambert. It was released on January 14, 2013 as the fourth single from Lambert's album, _Four the Record_ (2011). "Mama's Broken Heart" was written by Brandy Clark, Shane McAnally, and Kacey Musgraves, and is about a woman losing control after a break-up and ignoring her mother's advice on dealing with such a situation.
The song garnered a positive reception from critics who praised the production and Lambert's delivery of the lyrics. "Mama's Broken Heart" peaked at number 2 on both the _Billboard_Country Airplay and Hot Country Songs charts respectively. It also charted at number 20 on the Hot 100, her fourth top 40 hit on that chart. The song was certified Platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America and has sold 1,960,000 copies in the United States as of September 2015. It achieved similar chart success in Canada, peaking at number one on the Country chart and number 30 on the Canadian Hot 100.
The accompanying music video for the song was directed by Trey Fanjoy.
texts.1:
"Mama's Broken Heart" is a moderate uptempo song in the key of E minor[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-2) written by Brandy Clark, Shane McAnally, and Kacey Musgraves. The song's female narrator acts out as she struggles with a break-up, which leads people to begin taking notice of her behavior ("Word got around to the barflies and the Baptists"). When her mother finds out, she responds by scolding her daughter and telling her to regain her composure ("Run and hide your crazy and start actin’ like a lady"). The second verse states that the narrator sacrifices her "spotless reputation" in favor of "revenge," which is in contrast with the way her mother's generation handled such situations ("Where you get a grip and bite your lip just to save a little face"), but ultimately she takes matters into her own hands because "[it isn't her] mama's broken heart."
Lambert, in an interview with Taste of Country, said that "Mama's Broken Heart" was the one song on _Four the Record_ she couldn't live without, and that she can relate to the character in the song: "I think we all have at some point or another. Mostly when we’re young. Especially crazy teenage love — you think the world is ending if you break up." She expressed that when she first heard it, "she knew it was special" and wished she had been the one to write it.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-3)
texts.2:
Musgraves, who grew up with Lambert, was reluctant to give her old friend the song, who was pitched it without Musgraves' consent. At her wedding, Lambert asked if Musgraves was going to record the song or if she could have it. Lambert said she had to "actually beg for this song." Musgraves gave it to her on the stipulation that she could sing background vocals, which she did.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-Musgraves-4) Tensions lingered between the two singers over the song, which Musgraves said she resolved when bringing Lambert into the collaborative process on her 2026 album, _Middle of Nowhere_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-5)
The song received favorable reviews from critics. Ben Foster of Country Universe praised the track, referring favorably to its "deceptively deep" lyrics, Lambert's delivery, and an "engaging [and] off-beat arrangement." Foster rated the song an A, and dubbed it Lambert's best single since 2010's "The House That Built Me."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-6) Taste of Country's Billy Dukes awarded the song 4 and 1/2 stars out of 5, comparing it favorably to Lambert's previous hits "Kerosene" and "Gunpowder & Lead" and favorably commenting on the sparse yet suspenseful nature of the production.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-7)

## Commercial performance
[edit]
"Mama's Broken Heart" debuted at number 54 on the U.S. _Billboard_Country Airplay chart for the week ending January 5, 2013, and debuted at number 46 on the U.S. _Billboard_Hot Country Songs chart for the week ending January 12, 2013. It also debuted at number 89 on the U.S. _Billboard_Hot 100 chart for the week of February 9, 2013, and at number 76 on the Canadian Hot 100 chart for the week of February 9, 2013. The song became Lambert's highest-peaking single on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, reaching number 20 until 2014's "[Somethin' Bad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somethin'_Bad "Somethin' Bad")" made it her second highest-peaking single on that chart.
The song has sold 1,960,000 copies in the US as of September 2015.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-sales-8)
The music video was directed by Trey Fanjoy and premiered in March 2013.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-9)

"**Mama's Broken Heart**" is a song recorded by American country music artist Miranda Lambert. It was released on January 14, 2013 as the fourth single from Lambert's album, _Four the Record_ (2011). "Mama's Broken Heart" was written by Brandy Clark, Shane McAnally, and Kacey Musgraves, and is about a woman losing control after a break-up and ignoring her mother's advice on dealing with such a situation.
The song garnered a positive reception from critics who praised the production and Lambert's delivery of the lyrics. "Mama's Broken Heart" peaked at number 2 on both the _Billboard_Country Airplay and Hot Country Songs charts respectively. It also charted at number 20 on the Hot 100, her fourth top 40 hit on that chart. The song was certified Platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America and has sold 1,960,000 copies in the United States as of September 2015. It achieved similar chart success in Canada, peaking at number one on the Country chart and number 30 on the Canadian Hot 100.
The accompanying music video for the song was directed by Trey Fanjoy.

"Mama's Broken Heart" is a moderate uptempo song in the key of E minor[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-2) written by Brandy Clark, Shane McAnally, and Kacey Musgraves. The song's female narrator acts out as she struggles with a break-up, which leads people to begin taking notice of her behavior ("Word got around to the barflies and the Baptists"). When her mother finds out, she responds by scolding her daughter and telling her to regain her composure ("Run and hide your crazy and start actin’ like a lady"). The second verse states that the narrator sacrifices her "spotless reputation" in favor of "revenge," which is in contrast with the way her mother's generation handled such situations ("Where you get a grip and bite your lip just to save a little face"), but ultimately she takes matters into her own hands because "[it isn't her] mama's broken heart."
Lambert, in an interview with Taste of Country, said that "Mama's Broken Heart" was the one song on _Four the Record_ she couldn't live without, and that she can relate to the character in the song: "I think we all have at some point or another. Mostly when we’re young. Especially crazy teenage love — you think the world is ending if you break up." She expressed that when she first heard it, "she knew it was special" and wished she had been the one to write it.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-3)

Musgraves, who grew up with Lambert, was reluctant to give her old friend the song, who was pitched it without Musgraves' consent. At her wedding, Lambert asked if Musgraves was going to record the song or if she could have it. Lambert said she had to "actually beg for this song." Musgraves gave it to her on the stipulation that she could sing background vocals, which she did.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-Musgraves-4) Tensions lingered between the two singers over the song, which Musgraves said she resolved when bringing Lambert into the collaborative process on her 2026 album, _Middle of Nowhere_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-5)
The song received favorable reviews from critics. Ben Foster of Country Universe praised the track, referring favorably to its "deceptively deep" lyrics, Lambert's delivery, and an "engaging [and] off-beat arrangement." Foster rated the song an A, and dubbed it Lambert's best single since 2010's "The House That Built Me."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-6) Taste of Country's Billy Dukes awarded the song 4 and 1/2 stars out of 5, comparing it favorably to Lambert's previous hits "Kerosene" and "Gunpowder & Lead" and favorably commenting on the sparse yet suspenseful nature of the production.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-7)

## Commercial performance
[edit]
"Mama's Broken Heart" debuted at number 54 on the U.S. _Billboard_Country Airplay chart for the week ending January 5, 2013, and debuted at number 46 on the U.S. _Billboard_Hot Country Songs chart for the week ending January 12, 2013. It also debuted at number 89 on the U.S. _Billboard_Hot 100 chart for the week of February 9, 2013, and at number 76 on the Canadian Hot 100 chart for the week of February 9, 2013. The song became Lambert's highest-peaking single on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, reaching number 20 until 2014's "[Somethin' Bad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somethin'_Bad "Somethin' Bad")" made it her second highest-peaking single on that chart.
The song has sold 1,960,000 copies in the US as of September 2015.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-sales-8)
The music video was directed by Trey Fanjoy and premiered in March 2013.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart#cite_note-9)

When Blake Shelton married Miranda Lambert in May, they invited a lot of their Nashville friends to the ceremony in Texas. Among the guests was Chris Young, who shared his experiences with Country Countdown USA’s Lon Helton: “Amazing, first of all. It was just gorgeous. I wish I had a girl here to describe it. Girls are better at describing weddings that guys. Guys are like, ‘Yeah it was good.’ They’re like, ‘What color did the bridesmaids wear?’ ‘I Don’t know, I just know it was good!’ But it was a beautiful wedding, Blake sang a song to Miranda, Neal McCoy was the reception band, which is awesome because Neal is so cool. But it was the wedding of the year! Most memorable moment for me was they were keeping it private. Their were buses taking us everywhere. So we were on the bus and it was like all of country music was on this bus.Charles of Lady A, Dierks, everybody from Sony, it was really all of Nashville on these buses.”
LISTEN:11-30 Chris4
There is an amazing connection between Chris Young and Blake Shelton. It’s a connection that goes back to when Chris was just a teenager. He told CCUSA’s Lon Helton: “I used to go watch Blake with my parents when I wa sa kid, before he broke out and had his first hits. Like when he was playing the Gibson Bluegrass Showcase at Opry Mills, just him and a guitar. We saw four or five of his shows. I thought he was such a great singer. So when he won the CMA Male Vocalist award was so cool. He’s just an amazing vocalist.” Lon asked what was the reason Chris & his family went to see Blake before he had hits? “We just liked Blake and my sister had a crush on him.”

# Chris Young Sets The Record Straight
BySamantha Dawn Mutschler/ July 21, 2015
Early this morning **TMZ** reported rumors that **Miranda Lambert**‘s alleged affair with **Chris Young** and another man, not in the music business, were the cause of her split with husband **Blake Shelton**.
While Young is generally not one to entertain the rumor mills, he felt the need to address the situation before the conversations escalated:
Fans of Lambert and Shelton have been up in arms over the celebrity split and a sense of blame was starting to set inappropriately on Young. It’s no secret that Lambert and Young, label mates, who also once shared a manager, are friends. To most it’s also common knowledge that Young and Shelton share a bromance, often tweeting each other little digs and sharing affection in public.TMZ has since removed Young’s name from their original article.
(correction: at the time the article was written it seemed TMZ had removed Young’s name- sources confirm it has since been added back)
We hope that Miranda and Blake can manage some privacy and compassion during this time and Chris’s name be wiped clean from the slate of judgement before anymore damage is done. Continued prayers and thoughts to all involved.

# Chris Young Sets The Record Straight
BySamantha Dawn Mutschler/ July 21, 2015
Early this morning **TMZ** reported rumors that **Miranda Lambert**‘s alleged affair with **Chris Young** and another man, not in the music business, were the cause of her split with husband **Blake Shelton**.
While Young is generally not one to entertain the rumor mills, he felt the need to address the situation before the conversations escalated:
Fans of Lambert and Shelton have been up in arms over the celebrity split and a sense of blame was starting to set inappropriately on Young. It’s no secret that Lambert and Young, label mates, who also once shared a manager, are friends. To most it’s also common knowledge that Young and Shelton share a bromance, often tweeting each other little digs and sharing affection in public.TMZ has since removed Young’s name from their original article.
(correction: at the time the article was written it seemed TMZ had removed Young’s name- sources confirm it has since been added back)
We hope that Miranda and Blake can manage some privacy and compassion during this time and Chris’s name be wiped clean from the slate of judgement before anymore damage is done. Continued prayers and thoughts to all involved.

When Blake Shelton married Miranda Lambert in May, they invited a lot of their Nashville friends to the ceremony in Texas. Among the guests was Chris Young, who shared his experiences with Country Countdown USA’s Lon Helton: “Amazing, first of all. It was just gorgeous. I wish I had a girl here to describe it. Girls are better at describing weddings that guys. Guys are like, ‘Yeah it was good.’ They’re like, ‘What color did the bridesmaids wear?’ ‘I Don’t know, I just know it was good!’ But it was a beautiful wedding, Blake sang a song to Miranda, Neal McCoy was the reception band, which is awesome because Neal is so cool. But it was the wedding of the year! Most memorable moment for me was they were keeping it private. Their were buses taking us everywhere. So we were on the bus and it was like all of country music was on this bus.Charles of Lady A, Dierks, everybody from Sony, it was really all of Nashville on these buses.”

# Chris Young Sets The Record Straight
BySamantha Dawn Mutschler/ July 21, 2015
Early this morning **TMZ** reported rumors that **Miranda Lambert**‘s alleged affair with **Chris Young** and another man, not in the music business, were the cause of her split with husband **Blake Shelton**.
While Young is generally not one to entertain the rumor mills, he felt the need to address the situation before the conversations escalated:
Fans of Lambert and Shelton have been up in arms over the celebrity split and a sense of blame was starting to set inappropriately on Young. It’s no secret that Lambert and Young, label mates, who also once shared a manager, are friends. To most it’s also common knowledge that Young and Shelton share a bromance, often tweeting each other little digs and sharing affection in public.TMZ has since removed Young’s name from their original article.
(correction: at the time the article was written it seemed TMZ had removed Young’s name- sources confirm it has since been added back)
We hope that Miranda and Blake can manage some privacy and compassion during this time and Chris’s name be wiped clean from the slate of judgement before anymore damage is done. Continued prayers and thoughts to all involved.

**Miranda Leigh Lambert McLoughlin**(née **Lambert**; formerly **Shelton**; born November 10, 1983)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-3) is an American country music singer–songwriter. Born in Longview, Texas, she started out in early 2001 when she released her self-titled debut album independently. In 2003, she finished in third place on the television program _Nashville Star_, a singing competition that aired on the USA Network. Outside her solo career, she is a member of the Pistol Annies, a group she formed in 2011 alongside Ashley Monroe and Angaleena Presley. Lambert has been honored by the Grammy Awards, the Academy of Country Music Awards and the Country Music Association Awards. Lambert has been honored with more Academy of Country Music Awards than any artist in history. In 2024, Lambert was awarded the Country Icon Award at the [People's Choice Country Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Choice_Awards#People's_Choice_Country_Awards "People's Choice Awards").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-4)
After signing with Epic Records, she released _Kerosene_ in 2005, her first Epic album and second overall. It was certified Platinum in the United States and produced the singles "Me and Charlie Talking", "Bring Me Down", "Kerosene" and "New Strings". All four singles reached the top 40 on the _Billboard_Hot Country Songs. Her second album, _Crazy Ex-Girlfriend_, was released in early 2007. Three of its singles ("Famous in a Small Town", "Gunpowder & Lead" and "More Like Her") peaked within the top 20 on the country songs chart, with "Gunpowder & Lead" becoming her first top 10 entry in July 2008. Her third album, _Revolution_, was released in September 2009. Two of its songs – "The House That Built Me" and "Heart Like Mine" – topped the Hot Country Songs chart.

2011's _Four the Record_ included the singles "Baggage Claim", "Over You", "Fastest Girl in Town", "[Mama's Broken Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart "Mama's Broken Heart")" and "All Kinds of Kinds". Lambert released her fifth album, _Platinum_, in 2014.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-ReferenceA-5) The record won the Grammy Award for Best Country Album, and the album's lead single, "Automatic", reached the top five on the Country charts.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-6) Her sixth studio album, _The Weight of These Wings_, was released on November 18, 2016, and subsequently certified Platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-RIAA_Certification-7) Her seventh studio album, _Wildcard_, was released on November 1, 2019, and went on to win the Grammy Award for Best Country Album in early 2021. Three singles from the album ("It All Comes Out in the Wash", "Bluebird", "Settling Down") reached the top 20 of the country music charts, and the album's second official single, "Bluebird", became Lambert's first song to top the Billboard Country Airplay Chart as a solo artist since 2012.

She later collaborated with singer-songwriters Jon Randall and Jack Ingram for the album _The Marfa Tapes_, departing from her usual sound and opting for an acoustic, stripped-down feel. It was released on May 7, 2021, to acclaim from critics. Lambert released her eighth solo album, _Palomino_, on April 29, 2022. The same year she was listed on Time 100 by _Time_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-8) Lambert co-wrote and co-produced "[Choosin' Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choosin'_Texas "Choosin' Texas")", a 2025 single by Ella Langley that is the longest-running number one on the Billboard Hot 100.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-9)
Miranda Leigh Lambert was born November 10, 1983,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-dob-1) to Rick and Bev (née Hughes) Lambert in Longview, Texas,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-Miranda_Lambert_Biography-2) and was raised in Lindale, Texas. She was named after her great-grandmother, Lucy Miranda.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-usmagazine.com-10) She has one younger brother.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-11)

Her parents met while her mother was attending camp at Southern Methodist University where her father was an on-campus undercover narcotics officer, and they got together a few years later.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:0-12) Her father is a former Dallas police officer who played in a country-rock group called Contraband in the 1970s.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-13) Her parents later became private detectives and were hired by lawyers for Paula Jones in the Clinton v. Jones case. After the oil crisis dampened the economy in Texas, her family lost everything.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:0-12)
After the downturn, things got better and her parents began a faith-based ministry and offered their home as a shelter for the victims of domestic violence and their children. Miranda has said that this experience fueled her music and that her song "Gunpowder & Lead" is a reflection of that.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-14)
While still in high school, Lambert made her professional singing debut with "The Texas Pride Band".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-15) She also fronted the house band at the Reo Palm Isle in Longview, Texas,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-16) a long-running venue that had featured Elvis Presley and Willie Nelson, and the place where Brooks & Dunn started out as the house band.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-17)

### 2000–2003: Career beginnings, self-titled debut album, and _Nashville Star_
[edit]
Lambert performing at Laughlin AFB in 2006
At 16, Lambert appeared on the Johnnie High Country Music Revue in Arlington, Texas, the same talent show that had helped launch the career of LeAnn Rimes.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-18) Lambert then acquired a recording session in Nashville, Tennessee, but left the studio after she became frustrated with the "pop" type of music presented to her. She went back to Texas in 2000 and asked her father to teach her how to play guitar, so she could write her own songs.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-wrangler-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-20) In 2001, she released her self-titled debut album that consisted of 10 tracks.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:1-22)
In 2002, Dusty Meador hired Lambert to perform at Tye Phelps' country music restaurant and venue Love and War in Texas. Lambert continued to perform around the Texas Music Scene opening for Cooder Graw, Kevin Fowler, and Jack Ingram. In 2003, she auditioned for the talent competition _Nashville Star_, where she earned a third-place finish behind Buddy Jewell and John Arthur Martinez.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-23) During her 9-week stay on _Nashville Star_, Lambert caught the attention of the show's judge and Sony Music executive, Tracy Gershon, who later convinced the label to sign her.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-24)

### 2004–2008: _Kerosene_ and _Crazy Ex- Girlfriend_
[edit]
On September 15, 2003, she signed with Epic Records.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-about1-25) Her debut single, "Me and Charlie Talking", co-written by her father and Heather Little, was released in summer of 2004 as the lead single to her first Epic album, titled _Kerosene_. This album was also her first to be produced by Frank Liddell, best known for his work with his wife Lee Ann Womack and David Nail. Lambert wrote 11 of the album's 12 songs. The album debuted at number one on the _Billboard_Top Country Albums charts,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-26) and eventually gained a Platinum certification by the RIAA for shipments of over one million copies,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-27) selling more than 930,000 copies up to July 2008.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-28) Overall, the album produced four Top 40 singles on the _Billboard_ country charts, including the title track that became a Top 20 hit. Lambert also toured with Keith Urban[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-29) and George Strait[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-30) in early 2006. In 2007, she toured with Dierks Bentley and Toby Keith. On Thursday, August 7, 2007 Miranda played at the famous Sikeston Jaycee Bootheel Rodeo in Sikeston, Missouri.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-31)
Lambert on stage, in Pontiac, Michigan, March 31, 2007

### 2004–2008: _Kerosene_ and _Crazy Ex- Girlfriend_
Lambert's second album, _Crazy Ex-Girlfriend_, was released on May 1, 2007. She wrote eight of the album's 11 tracks,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-32) including its four singles. Much of the track "Gunpowder & Lead", the album's third single and her highest-charting single, was written while she was taking a concealed-carry handgun class in her home town.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-33) Fady Joudah of _The New Yorker_ said the album proved "she has talent and charisma on a par with Dolly Parton, another blond beauty who was once underestimated."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-34)

**Miranda Leigh Lambert McLoughlin**(née **Lambert**; formerly **Shelton**; born November 10, 1983)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-3) is an American country music singer–songwriter. Born in Longview, Texas, she started out in early 2001 when she released her self-titled debut album independently. In 2003, she finished in third place on the television program _Nashville Star_, a singing competition that aired on the USA Network. Outside her solo career, she is a member of the Pistol Annies, a group she formed in 2011 alongside Ashley Monroe and Angaleena Presley. Lambert has been honored by the Grammy Awards, the Academy of Country Music Awards and the Country Music Association Awards. Lambert has been honored with more Academy of Country Music Awards than any artist in history. In 2024, Lambert was awarded the Country Icon Award at the [People's Choice Country Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Choice_Awards#People's_Choice_Country_Awards "People's Choice Awards").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-4)
After signing with Epic Records, she released _Kerosene_ in 2005, her first Epic album and second overall. It was certified Platinum in the United States and produced the singles "Me and Charlie Talking", "Bring Me Down", "Kerosene" and "New Strings". All four singles reached the top 40 on the _Billboard_Hot Country Songs. Her second album, _Crazy Ex-Girlfriend_, was released in early 2007. Three of its singles ("Famous in a Small Town", "Gunpowder & Lead" and "More Like Her") peaked within the top 20 on the country songs chart, with "Gunpowder & Lead" becoming her first top 10 entry in July 2008. Her third album, _Revolution_, was released in September 2009. Two of its songs – "The House That Built Me" and "Heart Like Mine" – topped the Hot Country Songs chart.
texts.2: 2011's _Four the Record_ included the singles "Baggage Claim", "Over You", "Fastest Girl in Town", "[Mama's Broken Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart "Mama's Broken Heart")" and "All Kinds of Kinds". Lambert released her fifth album, _Platinum_, in 2014.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-ReferenceA-5) The record won the Grammy Award for Best Country Album, and the album's lead single, "Automatic", reached the top five on the Country charts.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-6) Her sixth studio album, _The Weight of These Wings_, was released on November 18, 2016, and subsequently certified Platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-RIAA_Certification-7) Her seventh studio album, _Wildcard_, was released on November 1, 2019, and went on to win the Grammy Award for Best Country Album in early 2021. Three singles from the album ("It All Comes Out in the Wash", "Bluebird", "Settling Down") reached the top 20 of the country music charts, and the album's second official single, "Bluebird", became Lambert's first song to top the Billboard Country Airplay Chart as a solo artist since 2012.

She later collaborated with singer-songwriters Jon Randall and Jack Ingram for the album _The Marfa Tapes_, departing from her usual sound and opting for an acoustic, stripped-down feel. It was released on May 7, 2021, to acclaim from critics. Lambert released her eighth solo album, _Palomino_, on April 29, 2022. The same year she was listed on Time 100 by _Time_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-8) Lambert co-wrote and co-produced "[Choosin' Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choosin'_Texas "Choosin' Texas")", a 2025 single by Ella Langley that is the longest-running number one on the Billboard Hot 100.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-9)
Miranda Leigh Lambert was born November 10, 1983,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-dob-1) to Rick and Bev (née Hughes) Lambert in Longview, Texas,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-Miranda_Lambert_Biography-2) and was raised in Lindale, Texas. She was named after her great-grandmother, Lucy Miranda.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-usmagazine.com-10) She has one younger brother.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-11)
texts.4:
Her parents met while her mother was attending camp at Southern Methodist University where her father was an on-campus undercover narcotics officer, and they got together a few years later.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:0-12) Her father is a former Dallas police officer who played in a country-rock group called Contraband in the 1970s.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-13) Her parents later became private detectives and were hired by lawyers for Paula Jones in the Clinton v. Jones case. After the oil crisis dampened the economy in Texas, her family lost everything.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:0-12)
After the downturn, things got better and her parents began a faith-based ministry and offered their home as a shelter for the victims of domestic violence and their children. Miranda has said that this experience fueled her music and that her song "Gunpowder & Lead" is a reflection of that.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-14)
While still in high school, Lambert made her professional singing debut with "The Texas Pride Band".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-15) She also fronted the house band at the Reo Palm Isle in Longview, Texas,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-16) a long-running venue that had featured Elvis Presley and Willie Nelson, and the place where Brooks & Dunn started out as the house band.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-17)

### 2000–2003: Career beginnings, self-titled debut album, and _Nashville Star_
[edit]
Lambert performing at Laughlin AFB in 2006
At 16, Lambert appeared on the Johnnie High Country Music Revue in Arlington, Texas, the same talent show that had helped launch the career of LeAnn Rimes.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-18) Lambert then acquired a recording session in Nashville, Tennessee, but left the studio after she became frustrated with the "pop" type of music presented to her. She went back to Texas in 2000 and asked her father to teach her how to play guitar, so she could write her own songs.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-wrangler-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-20) In 2001, she released her self-titled debut album that consisted of 10 tracks.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:1-22)
In 2002, Dusty Meador hired Lambert to perform at Tye Phelps' country music restaurant and venue Love and War in Texas. Lambert continued to perform around the Texas Music Scene opening for Cooder Graw, Kevin Fowler, and Jack Ingram. In 2003, she auditioned for the talent competition _Nashville Star_, where she earned a third-place finish behind Buddy Jewell and John Arthur Martinez.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-23) During her 9-week stay on _Nashville Star_, Lambert caught the attention of the show's judge and Sony Music executive, Tracy Gershon, who later convinced the label to sign her.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-24)

### 2004–2008: _Kerosene_ and _Crazy Ex- Girlfriend_
[edit]
On September 15, 2003, she signed with Epic Records.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-about1-25) Her debut single, "Me and Charlie Talking", co-written by her father and Heather Little, was released in summer of 2004 as the lead single to her first Epic album, titled _Kerosene_. This album was also her first to be produced by Frank Liddell, best known for his work with his wife Lee Ann Womack and David Nail. Lambert wrote 11 of the album's 12 songs. The album debuted at number one on the _Billboard_Top Country Albums charts,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-26) and eventually gained a Platinum certification by the RIAA for shipments of over one million copies,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-27) selling more than 930,000 copies up to July 2008.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-28) Overall, the album produced four Top 40 singles on the _Billboard_ country charts, including the title track that became a Top 20 hit. Lambert also toured with Keith Urban[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-29) and George Strait[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-30) in early 2006. In 2007, she toured with Dierks Bentley and Toby Keith. On Thursday, August 7, 2007 Miranda played at the famous Sikeston Jaycee Bootheel Rodeo in Sikeston, Missouri.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-31)

### 2004–2008: _Kerosene_ and _Crazy Ex- Girlfriend_
Lambert's second album, _Crazy Ex-Girlfriend_, was released on May 1, 2007. She wrote eight of the album's 11 tracks,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-32) including its four singles. Much of the track "Gunpowder & Lead", the album's third single and her highest-charting single, was written while she was taking a concealed-carry handgun class in her home town.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-33) Fady Joudah of _The New Yorker_ said the album proved "she has talent and charisma on a par with Dolly Parton, another blond beauty who was once underestimated."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-34)
In 2005, at the 40th Annual Academy of Country Music Awards in Las Vegas, Lambert won the CoverGirl "Fresh Face of Country Music Award". She was also nominated for the Country Music Association's Horizon Award in 2005; in 2007, Lambert also received a Grammy Award nomination for Best Female Country Vocal Performance for her single "Kerosene". She also won the Top New Female Vocalist award at the 2007 ACM (Academy of Country Music) Awards. At the 2008 ACM (Academy of Country Music) Awards, _Crazy Ex-Girlfriend_ won Album of the Year.

**Miranda Leigh Lambert McLoughlin**(née **Lambert**; formerly **Shelton**; born November 10, 1983)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-3) is an American country music singer–songwriter. Born in Longview, Texas, she started out in early 2001 when she released her self-titled debut album independently. In 2003, she finished in third place on the television program _Nashville Star_, a singing competition that aired on the USA Network. Outside her solo career, she is a member of the Pistol Annies, a group she formed in 2011 alongside Ashley Monroe and Angaleena Presley. Lambert has been honored by the Grammy Awards, the Academy of Country Music Awards and the Country Music Association Awards. Lambert has been honored with more Academy of Country Music Awards than any artist in history. In 2024, Lambert was awarded the Country Icon Award at the [People's Choice Country Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Choice_Awards#People's_Choice_Country_Awards "People's Choice Awards").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-4)
After signing with Epic Records, she released _Kerosene_ in 2005, her first Epic album and second overall. It was certified Platinum in the United States and produced the singles "Me and Charlie Talking", "Bring Me Down", "Kerosene" and "New Strings". All four singles reached the top 40 on the _Billboard_Hot Country Songs. Her second album, _Crazy Ex-Girlfriend_, was released in early 2007. Three of its singles ("Famous in a Small Town", "Gunpowder & Lead" and "More Like Her") peaked within the top 20 on the country songs chart, with "Gunpowder & Lead" becoming her first top 10 entry in July 2008. Her third album, _Revolution_, was released in September 2009. Two of its songs – "The House That Built Me" and "Heart Like Mine" – topped the Hot Country Songs chart.

2011's _Four the Record_ included the singles "Baggage Claim", "Over You", "Fastest Girl in Town", "[Mama's Broken Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart "Mama's Broken Heart")" and "All Kinds of Kinds". Lambert released her fifth album, _Platinum_, in 2014.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-ReferenceA-5) The record won the Grammy Award for Best Country Album, and the album's lead single, "Automatic", reached the top five on the Country charts.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-6) Her sixth studio album, _The Weight of These Wings_, was released on November 18, 2016, and subsequently certified Platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-RIAA_Certification-7) Her seventh studio album, _Wildcard_, was released on November 1, 2019, and went on to win the Grammy Award for Best Country Album in early 2021. Three singles from the album ("It All Comes Out in the Wash", "Bluebird", "Settling Down") reached the top 20 of the country music charts, and the album's second official single, "Bluebird", became Lambert's first song to top the Billboard Country Airplay Chart as a solo artist since 2012.

She later collaborated with singer-songwriters Jon Randall and Jack Ingram for the album _The Marfa Tapes_, departing from her usual sound and opting for an acoustic, stripped-down feel. It was released on May 7, 2021, to acclaim from critics. Lambert released her eighth solo album, _Palomino_, on April 29, 2022. The same year she was listed on Time 100 by _Time_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-8) Lambert co-wrote and co-produced "[Choosin' Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choosin'_Texas "Choosin' Texas")", a 2025 single by Ella Langley that is the longest-running number one on the Billboard Hot 100.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-9)
Miranda Leigh Lambert was born November 10, 1983,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-dob-1) to Rick and Bev (née Hughes) Lambert in Longview, Texas,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-Miranda_Lambert_Biography-2) and was raised in Lindale, Texas. She was named after her great-grandmother, Lucy Miranda.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-usmagazine.com-10) She has one younger brother.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-11)

Her parents met while her mother was attending camp at Southern Methodist University where her father was an on-campus undercover narcotics officer, and they got together a few years later.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:0-12) Her father is a former Dallas police officer who played in a country-rock group called Contraband in the 1970s.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-13) Her parents later became private detectives and were hired by lawyers for Paula Jones in the Clinton v. Jones case. After the oil crisis dampened the economy in Texas, her family lost everything.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:0-12)
After the downturn, things got better and her parents began a faith-based ministry and offered their home as a shelter for the victims of domestic violence and their children. Miranda has said that this experience fueled her music and that her song "Gunpowder & Lead" is a reflection of that.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-14)
While still in high school, Lambert made her professional singing debut with "The Texas Pride Band".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-15) She also fronted the house band at the Reo Palm Isle in Longview, Texas,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-16) a long-running venue that had featured Elvis Presley and Willie Nelson, and the place where Brooks & Dunn started out as the house band.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-17)

### 2000–2003: Career beginnings, self-titled debut album, and _Nashville Star_
[edit]
Lambert performing at Laughlin AFB in 2006
At 16, Lambert appeared on the Johnnie High Country Music Revue in Arlington, Texas, the same talent show that had helped launch the career of LeAnn Rimes.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-18) Lambert then acquired a recording session in Nashville, Tennessee, but left the studio after she became frustrated with the "pop" type of music presented to her. She went back to Texas in 2000 and asked her father to teach her how to play guitar, so she could write her own songs.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-wrangler-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-20) In 2001, she released her self-titled debut album that consisted of 10 tracks.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:1-22)
In 2002, Dusty Meador hired Lambert to perform at Tye Phelps' country music restaurant and venue Love and War in Texas. Lambert continued to perform around the Texas Music Scene opening for Cooder Graw, Kevin Fowler, and Jack Ingram. In 2003, she auditioned for the talent competition _Nashville Star_, where she earned a third-place finish behind Buddy Jewell and John Arthur Martinez.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-23) During her 9-week stay on _Nashville Star_, Lambert caught the attention of the show's judge and Sony Music executive, Tracy Gershon, who later convinced the label to sign her.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-24)

### 2004–2008: _Kerosene_ and _Crazy Ex- Girlfriend_
[edit]
On September 15, 2003, she signed with Epic Records.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-about1-25) Her debut single, "Me and Charlie Talking", co-written by her father and Heather Little, was released in summer of 2004 as the lead single to her first Epic album, titled _Kerosene_. This album was also her first to be produced by Frank Liddell, best known for his work with his wife Lee Ann Womack and David Nail. Lambert wrote 11 of the album's 12 songs. The album debuted at number one on the _Billboard_Top Country Albums charts,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-26) and eventually gained a Platinum certification by the RIAA for shipments of over one million copies,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-27) selling more than 930,000 copies up to July 2008.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-28) Overall, the album produced four Top 40 singles on the _Billboard_ country charts, including the title track that became a Top 20 hit. Lambert also toured with Keith Urban[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-29) and George Strait[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-30) in early 2006. In 2007, she toured with Dierks Bentley and Toby Keith. On Thursday, August 7, 2007 Miranda played at the famous Sikeston Jaycee Bootheel Rodeo in Sikeston, Missouri.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-31)
Lambert on stage, in Pontiac, Michigan, March 31, 2007

### 2004–2008: _Kerosene_ and _Crazy Ex- Girlfriend_
Lambert's second album, _Crazy Ex-Girlfriend_, was released on May 1, 2007. She wrote eight of the album's 11 tracks,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-32) including its four singles. Much of the track "Gunpowder & Lead", the album's third single and her highest-charting single, was written while she was taking a concealed-carry handgun class in her home town.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-33) Fady Joudah of _The New Yorker_ said the album proved "she has talent and charisma on a par with Dolly Parton, another blond beauty who was once underestimated."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-34)
In 2005, at the 40th Annual Academy of Country Music Awards in Las Vegas, Lambert won the CoverGirl "Fresh Face of Country Music Award". She was also nominated for the Country Music Association's Horizon Award in 2005; in 2007, Lambert also received a Grammy Award nomination for Best Female Country Vocal Performance for her single "Kerosene". She also won the Top New Female Vocalist award at the 2007 ACM (Academy of Country Music) Awards. At the 2008 ACM (Academy of Country Music) Awards, _Crazy Ex-Girlfriend_ won Album of the Year.

Miranda Lambert's _Crisco_ album release is exciting for her husband Brendan McLoughlin, and not just because he's a supportive partner. He's also a pretty heavily credited songwriter on the project.
McLoughlin co-write five tracks on the album, including "Snakeskin Boots," which is a radio single and a duet between Lambert and Ella Langley.
**_Read More_: 16 Pics of Miranda Lambert's Husband, Brendan McLoughlin, Shirtless**
He's also listed as a writer on "Cowgirl Curtsy," "Two Things Can Be True," "Till the Going's Gone" and "Right Where We Left It." That means that McLoughlin had a hand in writing half the original material on the album! (_Crisco_ has 11 songs, one of which is a Jim Croce cover.)

# Why Miranda Lambert’s ‘Crisco’ Album is a Very Big Deal to Her Husband Brendan McLoughlin
### **Is Miranda Lambert's Husband Brendan McLoughlin a Songwriter?**
Historically, not really.
Brendan McLoughlin is a former NYPD officer who married Lambert in 2019. She's said in the past that he embraced life in Tennessee as well as her country music world. He frequently appears alongside her at industry events and on red carpets.
His enthusiasm about her world seems to extend into the songwriting process. He co-wrote her 2024 song "Dammit Randy," and Lambert later said he got a little emotional when he learned she decided to cut it.
"We cut it in the studio, he wasn't there all day, he came in in the afternoon," she recounted. "I was like, 'I wanna play you something.' The whole band knew he'd written it, so we're just staring at him...and we pushed play."

"He won't say it, but he got a little misty-eyed," she continued. "He's like, 'You cut my song?!' And it's one of my favorites on the record."

# Why Miranda Lambert’s ‘Crisco’ Album is a Very Big Deal to Her Husband Brendan McLoughlin
### **What Did Miranda Lambert's Husband Say About Writing Five Tracks On _Crisco_?**
After the album came out last week, Brendan McLoughlin shared a rare social media post to celebrate its release.
"So proud and excited for the release of _Crisco_," he said. "It was an honor to be able to be part of such an incredible album."
He also thanked Lambert and his fellow songwriters for "allowing me to crash your write in Napa and [contribute] to five amazing songs, including my first ever radio single."

### 2021–2022: _The Marfa Tapes_, _Palomino_, and Pistol Annies' _Hell of a Holiday_
The Pistol Annies announced the release of their first Christmas album, _Hell of a Holiday,_ which was released October 22, 2021.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-Price-79) It contains 10 original songs, a cover of Merle Haggard's "If We Make It Through December", popular Christmas classic "Sleigh Ride", and traditional New Year's song "Auld Lang Syne".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-Price-79) The album was well-received for its original content, and Billboard praised their cover of "If We Make It Through December" as "One of the most striking moments on _Hell of a Holiday"_.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-80) They performed many of the songs and discussed the album on December 15's "The Pistol Annies Hell of a Holiday Special", which was made available on Facebook.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-81)
On December 30, 2021, Lambert released "Y'all Means All" in support of the LGBTQ community. The song was used in the trailer for the sixth season of _Queer Eye_.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-82) In March 2022 she won Entertainer of the Year at the American Country Music Awards.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-83)

### 2021–2022: _The Marfa Tapes_, _Palomino_, and Pistol Annies' _Hell of a Holiday_
Lambert and Elle King's 2021 collaboration "[Drunk (And I Don't Wanna Go Home)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drunk_(And_I_Don't_Wanna_Go_Home) "Drunk (And I Don't Wanna Go Home)")" was certified platinum in February, and the two performed the song together at the Ryman Auditorium on Feb 28th to celebrate.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-84) The single has so far reached the top 10 of the country charts.
Lambert released a teaser for a new song titled "Strange" ahead of the ACM Awards, which were held on March 7 in Vegas. She was nominated for 5 awards, marking her record-breaking 16th nomination for Female Vocalist of the Year, and she won Video of the Year for "Drunk (And I Don't Wanna Go Home)", and as well as the top prize of the night, Entertainer of the Year, for the first time in her career.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-85) This brings her tally of total ACM Awards won to 37, the most of all time, and also meant that she is eligible for the ACM's rare and coveted Triple Crown Award.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-86)
On March 10, Lambert released "Strange" alongside a video on her YouTube channel, and announced her eighth solo studio album, _Palomino_, which was released on April 29.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-87) The album includes "If I Was a Cowboy" and "Strange", alongside three re-recorded tracks from her 2021 _Marfa Tapes_ album with Jon Randall and Jack Ingram: "Geraldene", "In His Arms", and "Waxahachie".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-88)

### 2021–2022: _The Marfa Tapes_, _Palomino_, and Pistol Annies' _Hell of a Holiday_
Lambert headlined Europe's largest country music festival, C2C: Country 2 Country, from March 11–13, 2022, marking her first performances in the UK/Europe since her headlining tour there in 2017. She performed two songs from _Palomino_ live for the first time ever at her London show on March 11, her single "If I Was a Cowboy" and "Actin' Up".[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-89)

### 2023–present: Label change, _Postcards from Texas_, and _Crisco_
[edit]
In March 2023, Lambert announced that she was leaving Sony Music Nashville after nineteen years.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-90)
In April 2024, Lambert announced that she had signed a joint deal with Republic Records and Big Loud, with the latter set to handle country radio promotion and marketing.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-91) She also announced the first single under the new contract, "Wranglers", which was released on May 3, 2024. It serves as the lead single to her tenth studio album, _Postcards from Texas_.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-92) Promotional single "Dammit Randy" was released on June 28, 2024, a song she co-wrote with her husband, Brendan McLoughlin.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-93) The album was released on September 13, 2024.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:1-22)
Lambert co-wrote and sang backing vocals on Ella Langley's 2026 No. 1 Billboard 100 hit, "[Choosin' Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choosin'_Texas "Choosin' Texas")." The song's video, set in a Texas bar, features Lambert as a country performer who takes a heartbroken Langley back to Tennessee. Lambert also co-produced Langley's album _Dandelion_ with her and Ben West, co-wrote and features on the track "Butterfly Season", and provides backing vocals on the track "You & Me Time".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-94)

### 2023–present: Label change, _Postcards from Texas_, and _Crisco_
On June 26, 2026, Lambert announced her tenth solo studio album, _Crisco_, would be released on October 2. The project sees Lambert expanding her sound and combining country music with elements of disco, and includes "A Song to Sing", her 2025 duet with Chris Stapleton.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-95)

Miranda Lambert's _Crisco_ album release is exciting for her husband Brendan McLoughlin, and not just because he's a supportive partner. He's also a pretty heavily credited songwriter on the project.
McLoughlin co-write five tracks on the album, including "Snakeskin Boots," which is a radio single and a duet between Lambert and Ella Langley.

He's also listed as a writer on "Cowgirl Curtsy," "Two Things Can Be True," "Till the Going's Gone" and "Right Where We Left It." That means that McLoughlin had a hand in writing half the original material on the album! (_Crisco_ has 11 songs, one of which is a Jim Croce cover.)

# Why Miranda Lambert’s ‘Crisco’ Album is a Very Big Deal to Her Husband Brendan McLoughlin
### **Is Miranda Lambert's Husband Brendan McLoughlin a Songwriter?**
Historically, not really.
Brendan McLoughlin is a former NYPD officer who married Lambert in 2019. She's said in the past that he embraced life in Tennessee as well as her country music world. He frequently appears alongside her at industry events and on red carpets.
His enthusiasm about her world seems to extend into the songwriting process. He co-wrote her 2024 song "Dammit Randy," and Lambert later said he got a little emotional when he learned she decided to cut it.
"We cut it in the studio, he wasn't there all day, he came in in the afternoon," she recounted. "I was like, 'I wanna play you something.' The whole band knew he'd written it, so we're just staring at him...and we pushed play."

"He won't say it, but he got a little misty-eyed," she continued. "He's like, 'You cut my song?!' And it's one of my favorites on the record."

### 2021–2022: _The Marfa Tapes_, _Palomino_, and Pistol Annies' _Hell of a Holiday_
The Pistol Annies announced the release of their first Christmas album, _Hell of a Holiday,_ which was released October 22, 2021.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-Price-79) It contains 10 original songs, a cover of Merle Haggard's "If We Make It Through December", popular Christmas classic "Sleigh Ride", and traditional New Year's song "Auld Lang Syne".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-Price-79) The album was well-received for its original content, and Billboard praised their cover of "If We Make It Through December" as "One of the most striking moments on _Hell of a Holiday"_.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-80) They performed many of the songs and discussed the album on December 15's "The Pistol Annies Hell of a Holiday Special", which was made available on Facebook.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-81)
On December 30, 2021, Lambert released "Y'all Means All" in support of the LGBTQ community. The song was used in the trailer for the sixth season of _Queer Eye_.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-82) In March 2022 she won Entertainer of the Year at the American Country Music Awards.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-83)
texts.22:
### 2021–2022: _The Marfa Tapes_, _Palomino_, and Pistol Annies' _Hell of a Holiday_
Lambert and Elle King's 2021 collaboration "[Drunk (And I Don't Wanna Go Home)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drunk_(And_I_Don't_Wanna_Go_Home) "Drunk (And I Don't Wanna Go Home)")" was certified platinum in February, and the two performed the song together at the Ryman Auditorium on Feb 28th to celebrate.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-84) The single has so far reached the top 10 of the country charts.
Lambert released a teaser for a new song titled "Strange" ahead of the ACM Awards, which were held on March 7 in Vegas. She was nominated for 5 awards, marking her record-breaking 16th nomination for Female Vocalist of the Year, and she won Video of the Year for "Drunk (And I Don't Wanna Go Home)", and as well as the top prize of the night, Entertainer of the Year, for the first time in her career.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-85) This brings her tally of total ACM Awards won to 37, the most of all time, and also meant that she is eligible for the ACM's rare and coveted Triple Crown Award.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-86)
On March 10, Lambert released "Strange" alongside a video on her YouTube channel, and announced her eighth solo studio album, _Palomino_, which was released on April 29.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-87) The album includes "If I Was a Cowboy" and "Strange", alongside three re-recorded tracks from her 2021 _Marfa Tapes_ album with Jon Randall and Jack Ingram: "Geraldene", "In His Arms", and "Waxahachie".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-88)
texts.23:
### 2021–2022: _The Marfa Tapes_, _Palomino_, and Pistol Annies' _Hell of a Holiday_
Lambert headlined Europe's largest country music festival, C2C: Country 2 Country, from March 11–13, 2022, marking her first performances in the UK/Europe since her headlining tour there in 2017. She performed two songs from _Palomino_ live for the first time ever at her London show on March 11, her single "If I Was a Cowboy" and "Actin' Up".[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-89)
texts.24:
### 2023–present: Label change, _Postcards from Texas_, and _Crisco_
[edit]
In March 2023, Lambert announced that she was leaving Sony Music Nashville after nineteen years.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-90)
In April 2024, Lambert announced that she had signed a joint deal with Republic Records and Big Loud, with the latter set to handle country radio promotion and marketing.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-91) She also announced the first single under the new contract, "Wranglers", which was released on May 3, 2024. It serves as the lead single to her tenth studio album, _Postcards from Texas_.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-92) Promotional single "Dammit Randy" was released on June 28, 2024, a song she co-wrote with her husband, Brendan McLoughlin.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-93) The album was released on September 13, 2024.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:1-22)
Lambert co-wrote and sang backing vocals on Ella Langley's 2026 No. 1 Billboard 100 hit, "[Choosin' Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choosin'_Texas "Choosin' Texas")." The song's video, set in a Texas bar, features Lambert as a country performer who takes a heartbroken Langley back to Tennessee. Lambert also co-produced Langley's album _Dandelion_ with her and Ben West, co-wrote and features on the track "Butterfly Season", and provides backing vocals on the track "You & Me Time".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-94)
texts.25:
### 2023–present: Label change, _Postcards from Texas_, and _Crisco_
On June 26, 2026, Lambert announced her tenth solo studio album, _Crisco_, would be released on October 2. The project sees Lambert expanding her sound and combining country music with elements of disco, and includes "A Song to Sing", her 2025 duet with Chris Stapleton.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-95)
